extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting preprints to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting scholarly preprints to the arXiv e-print repository, including allowed file formats, metadata rules, moderation, licensing, and scheduling of announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical and refereeable scientific contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv should be topical and refereeable scientific contributions that follow accepted standards of scholarly communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions are subject to a moderation process that verifies material is appropriate and topical. Material that contains offensive language, non-scientific content, or is plagiarized may be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered authors and endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: We only accept submissions from registered authors. If you are a new user or are submitting to a new category, you may be required to find endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must be registered; new users or those submitting in new categories should obtain endorsements as required by arXiv procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and content appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions are subject to a moderation process that verifies material is appropriate and topical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may remove material containing offensive language, non-scientific content, or plagiarized material. Submissions may be delayed by moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to distribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required rights grant for distribution via arXiv; authors must ensure licensing choices convey distribution rights to arXiv or grant the stated arXiv license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to arXiv terms of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must agree to arXiv terms of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of arXiv's submission terms is mandatory for all submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-submission expectation and third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to self-submit. Submissions by a third party are accepted under limited conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are specific instructions for third-party submissions and for index submissions (e.g., conference proceedings); consult those instructions when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and announcement schedule (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: New submissions received by 14:00 (Eastern Daylight/Standard Time Zone) are generally made available at 20:00 (Eastern) but are subject to delays in the moderation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission times affect announcement timing; delays in moderation can change availability. See the detailed schedule for exact windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference) and archival goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted submission formats (in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX, PDF, HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv's goal is to store articles in formats that are highly portable and stable over time; TeX/LaTeX is currently the best choice. Scanned documents are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly not accepted text formats
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv does not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source, and does not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting these formats; they will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats and processing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure formats: PostScript (PS, EPS) — requires LaTeX processing; JPEG, GIF, PNG or PDF figures — requires PDFLaTeX processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit figures and use the appropriate processing workflow for your figure formats. If submitting figures with (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., graphics, graphicx) so figures appear correctly. arXiv administration cannot provide TeX-related help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures or link externally
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, even if you provide links to view figures externally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures that are part of the submission must be included in the submission files themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File names containing other characters (e.g., spaces, question marks, asterisks) will be rejected. These restrictions are to ensure portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name and extension case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on arXiv's system. The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match the case exactly, regardless of whether your local system is case sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files (limited facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) that are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files for details and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the title and abstract for inclusion in metadata according to separate instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata (title and abstract) is used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching — ensure accuracy and conformity to the instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and correct your submission before final Submit Article step
rubrics_metrics.description: Before finalizing submission, carefully check the title and abstract (metadata) and the processed files, and correct any errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement, select the 'Unsubmit' icon to return it to incomplete status and allow modification; unsubmitting affects announcement scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit or replace submission (do not resubmit for corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before a submission is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. Do not make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Instead, replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed. Edits and final submission before 14:00 US Eastern Time Monday–Friday will not delay announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement frequency and mapping of submission windows to availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv are typically made public Sunday through Thursday, with no announcements Friday or Saturday. The page provides specific submission-window-to-announcement mappings (e.g., Monday 14:00–Tuesday 14:00 → Tuesday 20:00 → Tuesday night/Wednesday morning mailing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the detailed schedule to determine when a submission will be announced and when mailed to subscribers based on submission time (all times Eastern US).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact arXiv administrators for help
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need assistance with submission issues or discover errors, follow the provided contact procedures and use the Unsubmit workflow when appropriate.
